overview.title: 📖 Overview: A New Perek — The Tithing of Animals
overview.subtitle: Bekhorot 53a–53b
overview.hebrewSource: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: A new mishna opens the second half of Bekhorot: the mitzva of animal tithe (ma'aser behema) applies both inside and outside Eretz Yisrael, with or without a standing Temple, and to non-sacred animals but never to those already consecrated. It applies to cattle and flock animals, but the two categories are never tithed together, while sheep and goats — different species prohibited from crossbreeding — are tithed together as one 'flock.' The Gemara immediately probes each clause: how does this square with Rabbi Akiva's view limiting animal tithe sacrifice to Eretz Yisrael, and why, in practice, has the custom of tithing animals lapsed entirely in the post-Temple era?

slides.title: 🐑 The Mishna's Scope for Animal Tithe
slides.subtitle: Where, when, and on what animals it applies
rows: Both in and outside Eretz Yisrael
Both with and without a standing Temple
Non-sacred animals only, never already-consecrated ones
Tithed together — both are 'flock,' despite the diverse-kinds prohibition between them

slides.title: 🐂🐏 Squaring the Mishna With Rabbi Akiva
slides.subtitle: A baraita seems to limit animal tithe to Eretz Yisrael entirely

lines.speaker: Baraita
lines.text: Rabbi Akiva: the verse groups animal tithe with grain tithe (Deut. 12:6) — wherever you bring up grain tithe, you bring up animal tithe; nowhere else.

lines.speaker: Challenge
lines.text: That directly contradicts the mishna's claim that animal tithe applies outside Eretz Yisrael too!

lines.speaker: Resolution
lines.text: Not a contradiction — the baraita discusses bringing the tithed animal to Jerusalem to be SACRIFICED; the mishna discusses whether the animal becomes CONSECRATED at all.

lines.speaker: Result
lines.text: Outside Israel, the animal tithe is still holy, but only eaten by the owner once it develops a blemish — it can never be sacrificed there.

slides.title: 🚫 Why Animal Tithe Has Lapsed in Practice
slides.subtitle: Two competing explanations for the modern non-observance

nodes.content: ❓ If animal tithe applies even without a Temple, why does no one separate it today?
👶 Rav Huna: a decree due to concern for an 'orphan' — a baby animal whose mother died before birth, which is actually EXEMPT but might get mistakenly counted
❓ But that concern existed even when the Temple stood — and could always be solved by public announcement!
⚠️ Rabba's answer: the real reason is fear of mishap (tekala) — sanctified animals with nowhere to be sacrificed risk being used improperly, worked, sheared, or eaten unslaughtered

callout.label: Compare consecration generally:
callout.text: A baraita rules that today one should not consecrate, valuate, or dedicate items at all — and if one does, an animal must be locked away to die rather than risk misuse.

slides.title: 🔥 Firstborn vs. Tithe: Why the Difference?
slides.subtitle: If mishap is the concern, why still consecrate firstborn animals today?

boxes.title: Firstborn Animal
items: Consecration is automatic — it happens the moment it leaves the womb
Not within human control to prevent
Solution: sell the ears to a gentile in advance, or inflict a blemish before birth (R' Yehuda)

boxes.title: Animal Tithe
items: Consecration depends on a deliberate act of counting
One CAN avoid it by inflicting blemishes in advance — but no one knows which animal will emerge tenth
Blemishing the WHOLE herd risks leaving no fit animals once the Temple is rebuilt

callout.label: Final reasoning:
callout.text: For firstborns, ordinary (non-firstborn) animals remain available for future offerings; for animal tithe, blemishing an entire flock to avoid the decree would leave too few unblemished animals for sale or sacrifice.

slides.title: 🌾 One Kind Can't Cover Another
slides.subtitle: A principle borrowed from teruma, later applied to tithe itself

steps.content: 1️⃣ Mishna (Terumot): one may not separate teruma from one type of produce to exempt a different type — such teruma isn't valid teruma
2️⃣ Source: 'Give the best of THIS, and the best of THAT' (Numbers 18:12) — oil and wine, each separately
3️⃣ This is the seed of the same principle developed further on the next daf: distinct species cannot be tithed for one another

callout.label: Looking ahead:
callout.text: This teruma-based principle becomes the springboard for explaining exactly why cattle and flock, though both 'animals,' must be tithed as two separate categories.

summary.principle: Animal tithe applies broadly — everywhere and always — to consecrate every tenth non-sacrificial animal, but practical concern for misuse of holy animals without a Temple has led the Sages to suspend its observance entirely today.

flowSteps.content: 🐑 Mishna: animal tithe applies in/out of Israel, with/without Temple, to non-sacred herd and flock animals
🐂🐏 Herd and flock tithed separately; sheep and goats tithed together as one 'flock'

columns.content: 🚫 Practice lapsed today — Rabba: fear that sanctified, unsacrificeable animals will be misused
🌾 Borrowed from teruma: one species can never exempt another from tithing

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: consecration without a functioning Temple carries real risk, so the Sages suspended even a Torah-mandated tithe

quiz.q: According to the mishna, does the mitzva of animal tithe apply outside Eretz Yisrael?
o: No, it applies only within Eretz Yisrael
Yes, both inside and outside Eretz Yisrael, though only in Eretz Yisrael can the animal be sacrificed
Only during the Temple era
Only to firstborn animals
quiz.e: The mishna states animal tithe applies both in and outside Eretz Yisrael; the Gemara clarifies that outside Israel the animal is still consecrated but can only be eaten by the owner once blemished, never sacrificed there.

quiz.q: According to Rabba, what is the primary reason animal tithe is not practiced today, even though the Temple's absence alone wouldn't nullify the obligation?
o: Because animals no longer exist that qualify
Concern for a mishap (tekala) — sanctified animals with no altar to bring them to risk being misused
Because the Torah only obligated it during Temple times
Because there is no priest available to receive it
quiz.e: Rabba explains that consecrated animals which cannot be brought as offerings risk being sheared, worked, or eaten improperly — a general concern that led the Sages to suspend consecration of all kinds today, animal tithe included.

quiz.q: Why can one avoid firstborn consecration by inflicting a blemish before birth, but the same strategy is impractical for animal tithe?
o: Firstborn consecration cannot be avoided at all
One cannot know in advance which animal will emerge as the TENTH in the count, unlike a firstborn which is identifiable from birth
Animal tithe blemishing is entirely forbidden by Torah law
There is no connection between the two cases
quiz.e: A firstborn is identifiable from the moment of birth, but no one can know in advance which animal in a herd will turn out to be the tenth counted — so blemishing in advance isn't a practical option without blemishing the whole herd.

quiz.q: According to the mishna, are sheep and goats tithed together as one category?
o: No, they are always tithed completely separately
Yes — both are included under the single term 'flock' (tzon), despite being subject to the diverse-kinds prohibition with each other
Only during a leap year
Only if owned by the same person
quiz.e: The mishna teaches that the verse's term 'flock' (Leviticus 27:32) includes both sheep and goats as one category for tithing purposes, even though crossbreeding them violates the diverse-kinds prohibition.

quiz.q: What halakhic principle from the laws of teruma does the Gemara invoke regarding animal tithe on this daf?
o: Teruma may be estimated rather than measured precisely
One may not separate teruma (or by extension, tithe) from one type of produce to exempt a different type
Teruma must always be given to a Levite first
Teruma is exempt outside Eretz Yisrael
quiz.e: The Gemara cites the mishna in Terumot that one may not use teruma from one species to cover a different species — establishing the principle later applied to explain why herd and flock must be tithed separately.
